## sessionStart

VS Code Agents WindowのsessionStart hookを使い、新しいlinked Git worktreeの作成直後に初期化指示を自動注入する方法が示されている。最初に/worktree-initのような固定Skillを手入力せず、セッション開始時の初回ターンを統一できる。

## hooksの設定

まず、%USERPROFILE%\.copilot\hooks\を作成する。続いて同じ場所にworktree-init.jsonを置き、PowerShellから$HOME配下の.copilot/hooks/worktree-init.ps1を呼び出すよう設定する。呼び出しにはJoin-Pathが使われる。この設定により、新しいCopilotセッションが始まるとworktree-init.ps1が実行される。

## worktreeの判定

worktree-init.ps1では、Console.In.ReadToEnd()によって入力を読み取る。event.sourceの値がnewかどうかを確認し、event.cwdを文字列として扱う。さらにgitDirとcommonDirをTrim()した値で比較し、新しいlinked Git worktreeを判定する構成となっている。初回ターンへ指示を渡す前に、hook側で最小限のGit確認を行う。

## 初回ターン

自動注入される指示では、このターンが新しいlinked Git worktree作成直後の初期化ターンであることを明示する。ユーザーが最初に送信したテキストはセッションまたはworktreeのラベルにすぎず、タスク要求として解釈しないよう求める。あわせて、ファイルの変更、作成、削除、整形、移動を行わないことも指定される。これにより、ラベル入力を作業指示と誤認せず、初回の振る舞いを固定できる。
aa9c61b87065837b.bodyEn:
## VS Code Agents Window

VS Code Agents Window can standardize the initial turn immediately after creating a new linked Git worktree. Using a sessionStart hook removes the need to enter a fixed Skill such as /worktree-init manually and helps make session startup behavior consistent.

## sessionStart hook

First, create the directory %USERPROFILE%\.copilot\hooks\. In that directory, create %USERPROFILE%\.copilot\hooks\worktree-init.json.

The configuration assigns a PowerShell command that invokes the script through & (Join-Path $HOME '.copilot/hooks/worktree-init.ps1'). With this setting in place, worktree-init.ps1 is called whenever a new Copilot session starts.

This provides the automation point for checking the session and supplying the intended initialization behavior without requiring the user to submit the fixed Skill as the first input.

## New linked Git worktree

Next, create %USERPROFILE%\.copilot\hooks\worktree-init.ps1. The script reads its input with [Console]::In.ReadToEnd() and checks session information, including event.source and event.cwd.

The shown logic tests whether event.source is new. It also compares the trimmed values of gitDir and commonDir as part of determining whether the session follows the creation of a new linked Git worktree.

The hook therefore performs the relevant Git verification at session startup rather than relying on the user’s first submitted text to initiate that check.

## Fixed initialization turn

When the hook identifies the relevant situation, it injects a fixed initialization instruction into the first turn. That instruction establishes that the turn immediately follows creation of a new linked Git worktree.

It also defines the user’s first submitted text as only the session or worktree label, not as a task request. The instruction states that the hook has already completed the minimum Git verification and directs the agent not to modify, create, delete, format, or move any files.

The result is a consistent initial turn for newly created linked Git worktrees, with the startup instruction supplied automatically by the sessionStart hook.

chat.en: How does the sessionStart hook tell that it’s a new Git worktree?

chat.ja: 新規セッション時にPowerShellを呼び、Gitのディレクトリ情報を照合します。対象なら固定の初期化指示を初回ターンへ差し込みます。
chat.en: On a new session, it runs PowerShell and compares Git directory information. If it matches the target case, it injects a fixed initialization instruction as the first turn.

chat.ja: じゃあ、毎回「/worktree-init」って入力していた開発者が、同じ流れで始めやすくなるんだね？
chat.en: So developers who used to type “/worktree-init” each time can start with the same flow automatically?

chat.ja: うん。固定Skillの手入力を省き、新しいlinked Git worktreeでの開始時の動作をそろえる方法として紹介されています。
chat.en: Yes. It removes the need to enter that fixed Skill manually and keeps startup behavior consistent for a new linked Git worktree.

chat.ja: 新しいworktreeを見つけたら、最初の入力を作業依頼にせず、初期化から始める仕組みなんだね。
chat.en: Got it: when it finds a new worktree, it treats the first input as setup context rather than a task request.

chat.ja: そう。ただし対象は新しいlinked Git worktreeの新規セッションで、初期化指示ではファイルを変更しないよう定めています。
chat.en: Right. But it targets new sessions for newly linked Git worktrees, and the initialization instruction explicitly says not to modify any files.

8e28634cbe19a613.bodyJa:
Googleは、Gemini APIが提供するマネージドエージェント機能を拡張し、バックグラウンドでの非同期タスク実行やリモートMCPサーバーへの接続などの新機能を追加したと明らかにした。これにより、開発者はより高度な自律型AIエージェントを構築しやすくなる。

マネージドエージェントは、モデルの推論や外部ツールの呼び出し、状態管理などをGoogle側のインフラで肩代わりする仕組みで、開発者が複雑なオーケストレーションを自前で実装せずに済む点が特徴とされる。今回の強化で特に注目されるのが、時間のかかる処理をバックグラウンドで非同期に走らせられる点だ。従来はリクエストとレスポンスが同期的に結び付くことが多く、データ収集や多段階の推論といった長時間タスクは扱いにくかった。非同期実行に対応することで、エージェントが裏側で処理を継続し、完了後に結果を受け取るといったワークフローが組みやすくなると見られる。

もう一つの柱がリモートMCPサーバーへの接続だ。MCP（Model Context Protocol）は、AIモデルと外部データやツールを標準化された方法でつなぐためのプロトコルで、Anthropicが提唱し、業界全体で採用が広がっている。リモートのMCPサーバーに接続できるようになれば、社内システムやサードパーティのサービスをエージェントが利用可能なツールとして組み込みやすくなる。

背景には、単発の応答生成にとどまらず、複数ステップを自律的にこなす「エージェント型AI」への関心の高まりがある。OpenAIやAnthropicも同様に、ツール連携やエージェント構築向けの機能を拡充しており、各社が開発者の取り込みを競う構図となっている。今回のアップデートは、Geminiをそうしたエージェント開発の実装基盤として位置づけるGoogleの狙いを示すものと言えそうだ。

一方で、実運用に向けては留意すべき点も残る。バックグラウンドで長時間走るタスクはコストや実行時間の管理が難しくなりやすく、外部のMCPサーバーへ接続する際には認証やデータの取り扱いといったセキュリティ面への配慮も求められる可能性がある。開発者は新機能の利便性と運用上のリスクを見極めながら導入を進めることになりそうだ。
8e28634cbe19a613.bodyEn:
Google has expanded the managed agent capabilities within its Gemini API, adding support for background task execution and connectivity to remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, among other features. The update matters because it shifts more of the operational complexity of building autonomous AI systems from the developer to Google's infrastructure, potentially lowering the barrier to producing agents that can plan, act, and manage state over longer time horizons.

Managed agents refer to a server-side abstraction in which the platform handles the orchestration loop that an AI agent depends on: interpreting a goal, calling tools, evaluating results, and deciding on the next step. Rather than requiring developers to write and host this loop themselves, the Gemini API manages the runtime, tool invocation, and conversational or task state. The newly announced additions extend what those managed agents can do and how long they can run.

The headline change is asynchronous background task execution. Historically, many API-based agent interactions have been synchronous, meaning a client sends a request and waits for a response within a single connection. That model works for quick question-and-answer exchanges but becomes fragile for workflows that take minutes or longer, such as researching across many sources, processing large datasets, or coordinating multiple tool calls. With background execution, an agent can appear to continue working after the initial request returns, allowing developers to kick off a job, poll for status, or receive results later. This pattern is a common prerequisite for building agents that behave more like durable workers than momentary chat responses.

The second major addition is remote MCP server connectivity. The Model Context Protocol is an open standard, originally introduced by Anthropic in late 2024, that defines how AI applications connect to external tools, data sources, and services through a consistent interface. It has since gained broad adoption across the industry, with support appearing in offerings from multiple major model providers and developer tool vendors. By allowing Gemini's managed agents to connect to remote MCP servers, Google is enabling agents to reach tools and data that live outside the immediate application, using a standardized protocol rather than bespoke integrations. In practice, this means a developer could point an agent at an existing MCP server exposing, for example, a database, a ticketing system, or an internal API, and have the agent use those capabilities without writing custom glue code for each one.

Taken together, these features address two persistent challenges in agent development: longevity and interoperability. Background tasks tackle the problem of workflows that outlast a single request, while remote MCP support tackles the fragmentation that arises when every integration must be built from scratch. Google frames the combination as giving developers stronger building blocks for constructing capable autonomous workflows, though the practical reliability of any given agent will still depend heavily on prompt design, tool quality, and guardrails.

The move fits into a broader industry pattern. Competing platforms have introduced comparable primitives, including OpenAI's Assistants and Responses APIs and its Agents framework, as well as agent-oriented tooling from Anthropic, Microsoft, and various open-source projects such as LangChain and LlamaIndex. The convergence around MCP as a connective layer is notable, because it suggests the market is coalescing on shared standards for how models talk to external systems, which could reduce lock-in and make it easier to move agent logic between providers. Google's decision to support remote MCP servers rather than only proprietary tool definitions is consistent with that trend.

There are important caveats. Autonomous agents that run in the background and connect to external systems raise questions around cost control, observability, security, and the risk of unintended actions, since an agent acting on its own can consume resources or invoke tools without a human reviewing each step. Developers adopting these features will likely need to consider authentication for remote MCP connections, monitoring for long-running tasks, and limits on what agents are permitted to do. As with earlier agent tooling, the gap between a compelling demonstration and a production-ready system remains significant, and organizations are likely to proceed incrementally. Developers interested in the specifics should consult Google's official Gemini API documentation for supported regions, pricing, and current limitations, which tend to evolve as such features move from preview toward general availability.

chat.en: Think of MCP as a shared doorway for AI to interact with outside capabilities. This update makes it easier to connect to remote MCP servers.

bee242a6477cb421.bodyJa:
## LeRobot

NVIDIAとHugging Faceが連携し、オープンソースのロボット学習ライブラリ「LeRobot」に新たなモデルとフレームワークを追加する。高度なロボット学習システムの構築と展開に取り組む開発者にとって、導入の障壁を下げる提供内容と説明されている。

## 物理AI開発

オープンソースAIでは、モデル、データ、ツールの共有によって開発者が迅速に革新できることが示されており、ロボティクスにも同様の可能性があるとされる。一方、物理AIの開発では、大規模なデータセットをはじめとする高価で断片化したリソースが進歩を妨げる場合がある。今回の追加により、開発者がより高度なロボット制御を手軽に実装できる環境が整う。
bee242a6477cb421.bodyEn:
## New Models and Frameworks

NVIDIA and Hugging Face have partnered to add new models and frameworks to LeRobot, an open-source robotics learning library. The contribution matters because it is intended to lower barriers for developers building and deploying advanced robot learning systems.

The additions provide an environment in which developers can implement more advanced robot control more easily. According to the existing summary, the work combines contributions from NVIDIA and Hugging Face within LeRobot rather than introducing a separate robotics library.

## Open Source AI

The source says open-source AI has demonstrated how quickly developers can innovate when models, data, and tools are shared. It presents robotics as having the same opportunity through shared resources for physical AI development.

However, the source also says progress can be limited by resources that are costly and fragmented, including large datasets. The new LeRobot models and frameworks are positioned as contributions for the open robotics community, supporting more accessible development of robot learning systems.

chat.ja: LeRobotには、モデルだけじゃなく開発の仕組みも加わるの？何が入るのかな。
chat.en: Is LeRobot getting more than just a model? What exactly is being added?

chat.ja: Isaac GR00T 1.7という人型ロボット向けVLAモデルと、Isaac Teleopフレームワークだよ。VLAは画像や言葉から動作を考えるモデルのこと。
chat.en: It’s getting Isaac GR00T 1.7, a VLA model for humanoid robots, plus the Isaac Teleop framework. A VLA model uses visual and language inputs to determine actions.

chat.ja: じゃあ、ロボット開発者が学習や制御の道具をそろえやすくなる、ってこと？
chat.en: So does this make it easier for robotics developers to gather the tools they need for learning and control?

chat.ja: うん。LeRobot上で使える形にそろえることで、開発から導入まで進めやすい、より標準化された道筋になると説明されているよ。
chat.en: Yes. Bringing them into LeRobot is presented as a more accessible, standardized path from development through deployment.

chat.ja: 共有ライブラリにモデルと仕組みが集まって、ロボット開発へ入りやすくなるんだね。
chat.en: Got it—the shared library brings models and frameworks together, making robot development more approachable.

chat.ja: そうだね。ただし、Cosmos 3は近く追加予定とされていて、現時点で入ったとは書かれていないよ。
chat.en: Right. One caveat: Cosmos 3 is planned for a future addition, so it isn’t described as available in LeRobot yet.

今回示されている更新関係は、langchain-openai 1.6.6から1.6.7への移行である。メジャー番号とマイナー番号は1.6のまま維持され、末尾の番号が6から7へ進んでいる。

83fda40cd2c9d8ea.bodyEn:
## langchain-openai 1.6.7

langchain-openai 1.6.7 is a patch release of the OpenAI integration package, advancing it from version 1.6.6. It matters primarily as a potential dependency upgrade that teams can assess for adoption.

The release was published on September 30, 2026. Its recorded change is associated with #40933, which identifies the release update from langchain-openai 1.6.6 to 1.6.7.

## Changes since 1.6.6

The release information describes the update as “release(openai): 1.6.7” and links that change to #40933. It does not identify any additional package changes beyond the version advance recorded by that entry.

For teams managing dependencies, the available information supports treating 1.6.7 as a patch-level upgrade candidate. Evaluation can therefore focus on whether to move the OpenAI integration package from 1.6.6 to 1.6.7, using #40933 as the tracked release reference.

## Verified signature

The commit associated with the release was created on GitHub.com and signed with GitHub’s verified signature. This verification applies to the recorded commit connected with the release.

The release page also displayed several session and loading notices. These included messages about signing in, signing out, or switching accounts in another tab or window, each directing the user to reload the session. It additionally reported an error while loading, asked the user to reload the page, and stated that the requested action could not be performed at that time.

Those notices describe the state of the release page and session rather than an identified behavior of langchain-openai 1.6.7. The substantive release information remains the patch update from 1.6.6, its tracking under #40933, and the verified signature on the associated GitHub.com commit.

## 学習ループ

LeRobot v0.6.0は、ロボット学習における「想像・評価・改善」のサイクルを強化するリリースだ。行動前に未来を想像するポリシー、成功を判定する報酬モデル、失敗を学習データへ変える仕組みを組み合わせ、実機なしでの検証や反復的な性能改善を進めやすくした。

## 未来を想像

未来を想像してから行動するワールドモデルポリシーとして、VLA-JEPA、FastWAM、LingBot-VAが導入された。加えて、GR00T N1.7、MolmoAct2、EO-1、EVO1、Multitask DiTという新たなVLAにも対応する。想像に基づく計画を、ロボットのポリシーへ取り込める構成となっている。

## 評価と報酬

評価面では、RobometerとTOPRewardを扱う新しい報酬モデルAPIが追加された。さらに、6つの新しいシミュレーションベンチマークをlerobot-evalの下に統合し、想像や行動、成功判定を含む仕組みを測定できるようにした。深度センシングや、VLMを利用したデータセット注釈、独自の動画エンコーディングにも対応する。

## 失敗から改善

lerobot-rollout CLIは、DAgger方式の人間参加型修正を取り入れ、デプロイ時の失敗を訓練データへ変換する。これにより、実行結果を次の学習へ戻す改善ループを構成できる。訓練機能にはFSDPが加わり、HF Jobs上でのクラウド訓練も利用可能になった。インストールも、従来より大幅に軽量化されたと説明されている。
1ae5bbd48af43ba2.bodyEn:
## Closing the robot learning loop

LeRobot v0.6.0 focuses on a cycle of imagining, evaluating, and improving robot behavior. The release is intended to make validation and performance improvement easier, including work that can be done without physical hardware.

The central workflow combines policies that imagine future outcomes before acting, reward models that determine when a robot succeeds, and deployment tooling that converts failures into additional training data.

## Imagine the future

The release introduces world model policies that learn to imagine the future: VLA-JEPA, FastWAM, and LingBot-VA. It also adds a group of new VLAs comprising GR00T N1.7, MolmoAct2, EO-1, EVO1, and Multitask DiT.

These capabilities support imagination-based planning as part of the broader robot learning loop. Rather than treating action, evaluation, and retraining as isolated stages, LeRobot v0.6.0 brings them together in an iterative process.

## Reward models and evaluation

A new reward models API includes Robometer and TOPReward. These reward models provide a way to assess whether a robot has succeeded, supporting the evaluation stage of the workflow.

Six new simulation benchmarks are unified under lerobot-eval. They provide a common evaluation pipeline for measuring policies in simulation, making it possible to test aspects of robot learning without requiring a physical robot.

## Turn failures into training data

The lerobot-rollout CLI supports deployment with DAgger-style human-in-the-loop corrections. This allows failures encountered during rollout to be turned into training data, connecting deployment results directly to iterative policy improvement.

LeRobot v0.6.0 also adds depth sensing, VLM-powered dataset annotation, custom video encoding, FSDP training, and cloud training on HF Jobs. Alongside these training and data capabilities, the release provides a much leaner installation.

## クラウド間転送

SkyPilotとHugging Faceの統合により、モデルやデータセットをHugging Faceに保存したまま、GPUを確保できる任意のクラウドでAIワークロードを実行できる。データと計算環境が異なるクラウドに分かれた際に発生する、クラウド間の転送コストを抑えられる点が重要となる。

## Hubに保存

多くのチームでは、モデルやデータセットが単一クラウドの特定リージョンにあるバケットへ保存される一方、開発、学習、配信に利用できるGPUは別のクラウドに存在することがある。この状態では、自分たちのデータをGPUへ読み込むだけでもクラウド間の転送料金が発生する。今回の統合では、モデルとデータセットをHubに置き、計算処理をSkyPilotが担う形で両者を接続する。

## hf://でマウント

SkyPilotのジョブには、Hugging Face Bucketまたは任意のHubリポジトリをマウントできる。指定には1つの「hf://」URLと、すでに利用しているHF_TOKENを使う。そのうえで、GPUの空きがあるクラスタへジョブを起動する。これにより、保存場所をクラウドごとの計算環境へ合わせて移すのではなく、Hub上のデータを各ジョブから利用できる。

## ゼロ転送コスト

Hugging Faceはエグレス料金を課さないため、Hub上のデータを任意のクラウドにあるGPUへ読み込む際の転送コストは発生しないと説明されている。対象となる計算処理は開発、学習、配信であり、データやモデル成果物をHugging Faceに保持しながら、GPU容量を確保できるクラウドで実行できる構成となる。
e8ab18dce9562b48.bodyEn:
## Run AI Workloads on Any Cloud

SkyPilot now integrates with Hugging Face as a zero-egress storage backend, allowing teams to run AI workloads on any cloud while keeping datasets and model artifacts on Hugging Face. This matters when available GPUs are on a different cloud from the region where a team’s data is stored, a separation that can otherwise create cross-cloud transfer costs.

The integration supports compute for development, training, and serving. SkyPilot can run that compute on whichever cluster has the GPUs, while the associated models and datasets remain on the Hugging Face Hub.

## Models and Datasets Stay

For most teams, models and datasets live in a bucket located in one region of one cloud. However, the GPUs available for development, training, or serving may be on another cloud. Reading data from its original location onto those GPUs can therefore incur a cross-cloud transfer charge.

The SkyPilot and Hugging Face integration joins these two parts of the workload without requiring the models and datasets to leave the Hub. Teams can keep their data on Hugging Face while launching compute wherever GPU capacity is available.

## Mount a Hugging Face Bucket

A Hugging Face Bucket or any Hub repository can be mounted into a SkyPilot job. The job uses a single hf:// URL together with the team’s existing HF_TOKEN.

Once mounted, the data is available to the SkyPilot job running on the selected cluster. The same approach applies whether the compute is being used for development, training, or serving.

## Your Hub Data in Any Job

Hugging Face charges no egress fees, so reading Hub-hosted data onto the GPUs used by a SkyPilot job has no data transfer cost, regardless of the cloud running the compute. The result is a setup in which storage remains on Hugging Face and AI workloads can run wherever the required GPU capacity is available.

大規模言語モデル（LLM）を業務や日常の問い合わせに活用する動きが広がるなか、外部知識を的確に引き出して回答精度を高める技術が注目を集めている。arXivで公開された論文「VectorizationLLM」は、ベクトル化（埋め込み）技術を軸に、情報検索と応答生成の質を同時に改善するAIアシスタント手法を提案している。

ベクトル化とは、文章や単語を意味的な特徴を保持した数値ベクトルへ変換する処理を指す。似た意味を持つテキストはベクトル空間上で近い位置に配置されるため、キーワードの完全一致に頼らず「意味の近さ」で関連情報を探せる点が特徴だ。この仕組みは、外部文書を検索してからLLMに回答を生成させるRAG（検索拡張生成）の中核をなしている。

背景には、LLM単体では学習データに含まれない最新情報や組織固有の知識に答えられず、事実に基づかない「ハルシネーション」を起こしやすいという課題がある。RAGは回答生成の前段で関連文書を取り込むことでこの弱点を補う手法として普及が進んでおり、VectorizationLLMもこの枠組みを踏まえ、ベクトル化の精度や検索の効率化に踏み込んだものと見られる。

実装面では、PineconeやWeaviate、Milvus、Chromaといったベクトルデータベースや、埋め込みモデルを提供するOpenAI、Cohereなどのサービスが広く使われている。検索結果を並べ替えるリランキングや、意味検索と従来のキーワード検索を併用するハイブリッド検索を組み合わせて精度を高める工夫も一般的で、本論文の手法もこうした既存技術との比較や統合が論点になる可能性がある。

効率的な情報検索と応答生成の改善は、カスタマーサポートや社内ナレッジ検索、専門文書の要約といった実務での応用価値が高い。一方で、あくまで論文段階の成果であり、実運用での有効性や計算コスト、多言語対応などは今後の検証が求められる。ベクトル化を基盤にLLMの実用性をどこまで押し上げられるか、継続的な注目に値するテーマといえるだろう。
1514a316fae38046.bodyEn:
A new arXiv preprint titled "VectorizationLLM: A Smart AI Assistant Based on Vectorization" proposes a method for building large language model (LLM) assistants that lean on vectorization techniques to improve how relevant information is retrieved and how responses are generated. The work matters because retrieval quality is increasingly the bottleneck in practical AI assistants: as models are asked to answer questions grounded in private documents, technical manuals, or up-to-date data, the accuracy of the surrounding search pipeline often determines whether the final answer is correct or hallucinated.

At the center of the approach is the idea of turning text into numerical vectors, or embeddings, that capture semantic meaning rather than exact keyword matches. According to the summary, VectorizationLLM applies what the authors describe as "smart vectorization" to enhance both retrieval and response quality. In systems of this kind, documents are typically split into chunks, each chunk is converted into a high-dimensional vector by an embedding model, and those vectors are stored in an index. When a user asks a question, the query is embedded the same way, and the system retrieves the passages whose vectors are closest to the query vector, usually measured by cosine similarity or a related distance metric. Those retrieved passages are then supplied to the LLM as context so it can produce a grounded answer.

This design falls under the broader umbrella of retrieval-augmented generation, commonly abbreviated as RAG, which has become one of the dominant patterns for deploying LLMs in enterprise and research settings. RAG appeals to practitioners because it lets a model draw on information it was never trained on, reduces the tendency to fabricate facts, and can be updated by changing the underlying documents rather than retraining the model. The paper appears to position VectorizationLLM as a refinement within this space, focused specifically on the vectorization step that feeds the retrieval process. The exact technical contributions—whether a new embedding scheme, a reranking strategy, a chunking method, or a tighter coupling between retrieval and generation—would need to be confirmed from the full text, since the available summary does not spell them out.

It helps to place the work against the tools already common in this ecosystem. Vector databases such as FAISS, Milvus, Weaviate, Pinecone, and Chroma provide the storage and nearest-neighbor search that RAG systems rely on, while embedding models from providers and open-source projects convert text into the vectors those databases index. Orchestration frameworks like LangChain and LlamaIndex are frequently used to wire these components together. A paper proposing a "smart" vectorization approach is likely aiming to improve one or more weak points in this stack, such as retrieving passages that are topically close but not actually useful, handling long or heterogeneous documents, or better matching the granularity of stored chunks to the questions users ask.

Several persistent challenges shape research in this area and are worth keeping in mind when evaluating any new proposal. Embedding quality varies across domains, so a model that performs well on general web text may struggle with specialized legal, medical, or engineering language. Chunking decisions involve trade-offs between preserving context and keeping retrieval precise. Similarity in vector space does not always equal relevance to the user's intent, which is why hybrid approaches that combine dense vector search with traditional keyword search, along with reranking steps, have gained traction. Evaluating improvements is also nontrivial, since retrieval accuracy and answer quality are measured with different metrics and often require human judgment.

For readers, the significance of a paper like this is less about a single benchmark number and more about where it fits in an active line of research trying to make LLM assistants more reliable and cost-effective. If VectorizationLLM demonstrates measurable gains in retrieval precision or answer faithfulness, it would add to a growing body of work showing that careful engineering of the vectorization and retrieval layers can matter as much as the choice of the underlying language model. As with most preprints, the results have not yet been peer reviewed, and the strength of the contribution will ultimately depend on the datasets, baselines, and ablation studies presented in the full paper. Interested practitioners should look for reproducible code and comparisons against established RAG pipelines before drawing firm conclusions.

dc628bd8e0565517.bodyEn:
## Changes since LangChain 1.4.2

LangChain 1.4.3 adds support for Bedrock Mantle chat models and addresses several issues affecting structured output, fallback models, and agent tool calls. Together, these changes are intended to improve reliability in agent development.

The release follows LangChain 1.4.2 and includes a mixture of features, fixes, documentation corrections, dependency maintenance, and cleanup. Its main addition is support for Bedrock Mantle chat models in init_chat_model.

## Structured output and fallback models

LangChain 1.4.3 fixes recognition of GPT-6 structured output when profiles are not present. This change covers profile-free GPT-6 structured output recognition without introducing a requirement for profiles.

The release also sanitizes cache settings for fallback models. This fix specifically targets cache settings used in fallback situations, addressing how those settings are handled when fallback models are involved.

Both changes focus on model initialization and model behavior within LangChain. The structured-output fix concerns recognition without profiles, while the cache fix concerns settings associated with fallback models.

## Invalid tool calls

The release repairs invalid tool calls in create_agent. This correction directly addresses malformed or otherwise invalid tool calls encountered through that agent-creation function.

Alongside the structured-output and fallback-cache fixes, the create_agent repair forms part of the release’s reliability improvements for agent development. The scope described for this change is the repair of invalid tool calls rather than the addition of a separate agent feature.

## Documentation and dependencies

7930d29e761b7f7d.bodyEn:
## Unnecessary Git branches

A developer asked Cursor's AI agent to clean up unnecessary Git branches, but the task ended with all data under the D drive being deleted. The data did not remain in the Recycle Bin, making this a serious data-loss incident tied to an apparently limited Git cleanup request.

## Commands remain unidentified

The exact command could not be identified because both Cursor's chat history and the terminal history were also lost. According to the source, AI-assisted analysis suggested two possible causes: an unintended execution of “git clean -fdx,” or incorrect path resolution by a deletion command. Neither explanation was confirmed.

The source says similar incidents have been publicly reported with Claude Code and Gemini CLI. It therefore presents the risk not as specific to Cursor, but as a structural problem affecting AI agents more broadly. The case highlights the danger of giving an AI agent permission to execute destructive commands when an instruction can be interpreted beyond its intended scope.

## About page

Cline Desktop v0.0.37 adds a central place for update controls, release history, and support options. The change matters because users can check their installed version, review recent changes, update the application, and report problems from the same page.

The new About page in Settings displays the current version and channel. It includes Check for updates and Restart to update buttons, bringing both update discovery and the restart required to complete an update into that page.

Recent release notes are also listed there. Each entry links to its corresponding GitHub release, while a separate link provides access to the full changelog. Report an issue is available from the About page as well.

## What's new

After an update, a one-time What's new dialog summarizes recent features. The first dialog covers SSH remotes, worktrees, pull request status in the composer, and parallel sub-agents.

Although the dialog is presented once after an update, its contents remain accessible. Users can open Highlights on the About page to see the information again.

## Export Diagnostics

On macOS, the Help menu now provides a more direct route to diagnostics export. Choosing Help → Export Diagnostics… opens the diagnostics export directly.

This removes the previous need to locate the export option within Settings. Together with Report an issue on the About page, the change makes the relevant diagnostic and reporting actions easier to reach.

## Amazon Bedrock

The release also addresses an Amazon Bedrock failure involving OpenAI models reached through inference profiles. Profiles using us.openai.… or global.openai.… no longer fail with the message “Unknown parameter: 'reasoningConfig'” when reasoning effort is involved.

5e3f99e5cfa30c6f.bodyEn:
## New provider: ai&

Cline v4.1.21 adds a provider, refreshes its model catalog, changes some resolved default models, and improves how long replies from local models are handled. The release matters for users who rely on unpinned defaults or local models, because their selected model or task behavior may change.

The new provider is ai&, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint serving open-weight models from Japan.

## Refreshed model catalog

The refreshed catalog contains 6,386 models across 209 providers. Alongside that expansion, the resolved default model changes for 19 providers that do not pin a model.

Of those 19 providers, 11 now resolve to Claude Opus 5.5. The affected group includes GitHub Copilot and Vertex. Users who access one of these providers without explicitly pinning a model should therefore expect a different default model after updating.

These changes concern providers without a pinned model. Pinning a model avoids relying on the provider’s resolved default.

## Long replies on local models

The release also changes what happens when long replies on local models reach the output-token limit. This applies to llama.cpp, Ollama, and LM Studio.

Instead of ending the task at that point, Cline now compacts the conversation and retries once. According to the release, these servers cap generation according to the context that remains, regardless of the output budget configured by the user. The single retry is intended to reduce task interruptions when a reply reaches that limit.

## Minimum js-yaml version

Cline v4.1.21 raises the minimum js-yaml version to 4.3.2. This update picks up a security fix in the parser used to read rule and skill frontmatter.

fc5ae9be70c108b0.bodyJa:
## Bugs4Q

大規模言語モデル（LLM）を使って、バグを含むQiskit量子プログラムを自動修復し、その性能をBugs4Qで評価した研究である。量子ソフトウェア開発におけるLLMベースの修復について、可能性と現時点での限界を明らかにしている。

## 評価の前提

Bugs4Qは、実在する量子プログラムの欠陥を収録した、広く利用されているベンチマークとされる。一方、その評価では、ベンチマークに付けられたラベルが引き続き有効であることと、生成された修正が対象環境で実行できることが前提になる。本研究は、LLMが修正案を生成できるかだけでなく、こうした評価上の前提も含めて検証している。

## 67件の欠陥

評価対象はBugs4Qの2つのバージョンで、重複を除いた実在のQiskit欠陥67件が含まれる。実行可能なテストが欠けている項目にはテストを追加し、各項目を実際に再実行できる形で扱った。これにより、ラベルだけに依存せず、生成された修正が対象となるQiskit環境で動作するかを確認する構成となっている。

## 6つのリリース

全項目は、固定した6つのQiskitリリースで再実行された。対象は0.25.0、0.45.0、1.0.0、1.1.1、2.0.0、2.3.1である。複数のリリースを明示して検証することで、Bugs4Qを用いたLLMの修復性能を、実行環境と結び付けて評価している。研究は、量子プログラムの自動修復にLLMを適用する可能性を示す一方、現在の修復には限界もあるとしている。
fc5ae9be70c108b0.bodyEn:
## Repairing Qiskit Programs

The study evaluates large language models on automatically repairing buggy Qiskit quantum programs with the Bugs4Q benchmark. The work matters because it examines both the promise and the current limitations of LLM-based repair for quantum software, rather than treating generated fixes as correct without checking benchmark and execution conditions.

## Bugs4Q Benchmark

Bugs4Q contains real quantum defects and is widely used for evaluating repair approaches. The researchers assess two versions of Bugs4Q that together contain 67 unique real Qiskit defects. Their evaluation addresses an important assumption in the benchmark: that its labels remain valid when the entries are evaluated.

The study also considers whether generated fixes actually execute in the intended target environment. This makes execution part of the evaluation rather than relying only on benchmark labels.

## Executable Tests

The researchers add executable tests for Bugs4Q entries where such tests are missing. These tests support an evaluation of the defects and generated repairs through execution.

By combining the benchmark’s real Qiskit defects with executable tests, the study evaluates LLM-based repair against the programs themselves. Its methodology therefore covers both the benchmark labels and the ability to run fixes in the relevant Qiskit environment.

## Six Pinned Qiskit Releases

All benchmark entries are rerun across six pinned Qiskit releases: 0.25.0, 0.45.0, 1.0.0, 1.1.1, 2.0.0, and 2.3.1. Using pinned releases provides defined target environments for checking the Bugs4Q entries and the execution of generated fixes.

Through this evaluation across two Bugs4Q versions, 67 unique defects, added executable tests, and six specified Qiskit releases, the study presents evidence on the potential and present constraints of using large language models for automatic quantum-program repair.

chat.ja: 67件の実在するQiskitの欠陥を、6つのリリースで調べ直したんだね。これって大きいこと？
chat.en: They rechecked 67 real Qiskit defects across six releases. Is that a big deal?

chat.ja: 数だけでは決められないけど、全項目を複数環境で再実行し、ラベルや修正結果が有効か確かめた点が重要だね。
chat.en: The number alone doesn’t decide that, but rerunning every entry across multiple environments helps test whether the labels and generated fixes remain valid.

chat.ja: Bugs4Qって、そもそも何？ バグを集めた箱みたいなもの？
chat.en: What exactly is Bugs4Q? Is it like a box of bugs?

chat.ja: 近いよ。実在する量子プログラムの欠陥を集め、修復方法を同じ条件で比べるためのベンチマークだよ。
chat.en: Pretty close. It’s a benchmark—a shared set of real quantum-program defects used to compare repair methods under common conditions.

chat.ja: ぼくならQiskitのバグを見つけたら、LLMに修正案を考えてもらいたいな。すぐ使えるのかな？
chat.en: If I found a Qiskit bug, I’d want an LLM to suggest a fix. Could I use it right away?

chat.ja: 修正の可能性はあるけど、ラベルが正しいか、生成した修正が対象環境で動くかの確認が必要だよ。そこが示された限界だね。
chat.en: There’s promise, but you’d still need to verify the label and confirm the generated fix runs in the target environment. Those are key limitations highlighted here.

## v0.34.4

Ollama v0.34.4がリリースされた。断続的に発生する「model not found」エラーへの修正に加え、思考モデルの構造化出力、MLXでの画像解像度選択やプロンプト処理が更新され、ローカル利用時の信頼性と性能を高める内容となっている。

## 構造化出力

思考モデルでは、構造化出力を1回で適用するようになった。v0.34.4-rc1では、mlxrunnerが構造化出力に使用するXGrammarを0.2.7へ更新している。この更新により、型付き辞書の値と短い配列に関するスキーマ修正が取り込まれた。構造化出力を扱う際のスキーマ処理に直接関係する変更である。

## MLXの更新

MLXでは、Gemma 4の画像解像度を動的に選択する機能が加わった。画像解像度を固定的に扱うのではなく、動的な選択に対応する。また、Qwen 3.8ではプロンプト処理が高速化された。いずれもMLX上での処理に関する更新で、画像入力とプロンプト処理という異なる部分を対象としている。

## エラー修正

モデル検索では、断続的に起きていた「model not found」エラーが修正された。常に再現するとは限らない検索失敗への対応であり、ローカルでモデルを利用する際の信頼性向上につながると説明されている。今回の更新は、モデル検索の安定性、構造化出力の適用、MLX上の処理改善をまとめたリリースとなる。
d9eb9b12a750774d.bodyEn:
## Ollama v0.34.4

Ollama v0.34.4 focuses on reliability and performance for local users. The release fixes sporadic “model not found” errors, streamlines structured output, and introduces MLX changes for Gemma 4 and Qwen 3.8.

The model lookup fix addresses intermittent failures in which a model could not be found. By correcting these sporadic errors, v0.34.4 is intended to make local use more reliable.

## Structured outputs

The release applies structured output for reasoning models in a single pass. Its release material also identifies an mlxrunner update to XGrammar 0.2.7 for structured outputs.

That XGrammar update picks up schema fixes covering typed dictionary values and short arrays. These changes specifically concern how those schema forms are handled when producing structured output. Together, the single-pass application and the schema fixes are the release’s main structured-output changes.

The available release text labels the XGrammar change as part of v0.34.4-rc1. It describes the update as moving XGrammar to version 0.2.7 and directly connects that update with structured outputs.

## MLX

MLX receives two additional changes tied to named models. For Gemma 4, it adds dynamic selection of image resolution. This makes image resolution adaptive rather than using a single selection in every case.

For Qwen 3.8, MLX adds faster prompt processing. The stated improvement is specifically about prompt handling speed and is presented as a performance gain for local users.

Taken together, the MLX work covers adaptive Gemma 4 images, faster Qwen 3.8 prompts, and updated structured-output handling through mlxrunner. Alongside the fix for sporadic model lookup failures, these changes make reliability and performance the central focus of Ollama v0.34.4.

## 1.6.5の変更

langchain-openai 1.6.5がリリースされた。中心となる変更は、Opus 5.5とGPT-6のプロファイル拡張、およびSystemMessageを使った会話途中のツール変更で、AnthropicとOpenAIのエージェント開発者がモデルとツールをより柔軟に構成できるようにする内容だ。

## プロファイル拡張

今回のリリースでは、Opus 5.5とGPT-6に対するプロファイル拡張が追加された。変更履歴では「fix(anthropic)」として扱われており、langchain-openai 1.6.4以降の修正として収録されている。対象はモデルそのものの更新ではなく、Opus 5.5とGPT-6を扱うためのプロファイル拡張である。

もう一つの変更は、SystemMessageで会話途中のツール変更を可能にしたことだ。変更履歴では「feat(anthropic,openai)」に分類され、AnthropicとOpenAIの双方に関係する機能として示されている。会話開始時の構成だけでなく、会話が進行している途中でもSystemMessageを通じてツールを変更できる。

## ツール変更

この2つの更新により、エージェント開発者はOpus 5.5とGPT-6のプロファイル拡張を利用しつつ、会話中の状況に合わせてツール構成を変更できると説明されている。リリースには変更ごとの記録として#40785と#40758が示され、1.6.5のリリース項目には#40787が付されている。コミットはGitHub.com上で作成され、GitHubの検証済み署名で署名されている。

## langchain-openai 1.6.5

langchain-openai 1.6.5 was published on September 23, 2026. The release matters for Anthropic and OpenAI agent developers because it expands model profiles and allows tools to be changed during an ongoing conversation.

The listed changes are measured against langchain-openai 1.6.4. They focus on two areas: profile augmentations for specific models and greater flexibility in how tools are configured while a conversation is in progress.

## Profile augmentations

The release adds profile augmentations for Opus 5.5 and GPT-6. The change is identified as a fix for Anthropic and is associated with change number #40785.

These additions extend the profiles available through langchain-openai. According to the release summary, the result is more flexibility for developers configuring models in Anthropic and OpenAI agent projects.

## SystemMessage tool changes

A separate feature enables mid-conversation tool changes on SystemMessage. It applies to both Anthropic and OpenAI and is associated with change number #40758.

This means tool configuration is no longer limited to remaining unchanged throughout the conversation. Developers can make tool changes through SystemMessage after the conversation has already begun, providing more flexibility in how models and tools are configured together.

## Changes since 1.6.4

The release entry groups both updates under the changes since langchain-openai 1.6.4. The overall 1.6.5 release is associated with change number #40787.

The commit was created on GitHub.com and signed with GitHub’s verified signature. Taken together, the release’s stated changes cover new Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 profile support and the ability to adjust tools through SystemMessage in the middle of a conversation.

## v0.34.3

Ollama v0.34.3では、モデルごとの思考設定と既定値を確認する仕組みが追加され、Apple Silicon上での対応モデルも広がった。macOSアプリのウィンドウ動作やHugging Faceからのモデル取得に関する修正も含まれ、設定確認と運用を行いやすくしている。

## 思考設定

GET /api/showは、各モデルが提供する思考制御の選択肢と、その既定値を返すようになった。モデルごとに利用できる値が異なる場合でも、実行前に設定内容を確認できる。たとえばAPIの応答では、thinkingのvaluesとしてlow、high、maxが示され、defaultとしてmaxが返される形になっている。

## CLIとAPI

この情報はCLIからも確認できる。ollama showでgemma4のthinkingを表示する例では、思考レベルとしてfalseとtrueが示され、既定値はtrueとなる。APIではlocalhostの/api/showにモデル名を渡して確認でき、例としてglm-5.3-flash:cloudが使われている。クラウドモデルについては、ollama.comからも同じ情報を直接確認できる。

## MLXと修正

Nemotron H Visionモデルは、MLXを利用してApple Silicon上で動作するよう対応した。macOSアプリでは、閉じたウィンドウがアプリのアクティベート時に再び開かれないよう変更されている。また、Hugging Faceからのモデル取得に関する問題も修正された。変更範囲はv0.34.2からv0.34.3までの差分として案内されている。
976fbeee78eca770.bodyEn:
## What's Changed

Ollama v0.34.3 adds visibility into model thinking settings, expands vision-model support on Apple Silicon, and addresses issues involving model pulls and macOS windows. These changes make model configuration easier to inspect while smoothing several parts of model use.

## Thinking Controls

GET /api/show now advertises the thinking controls available for each model, along with the default setting. This information is available through both the CLI and the API.

In the CLI, running ollama show gemma4 displays the model’s thinking levels. The example lists false and true as the available values, with true identified as the default.

The API provides the same type of information. A request to http://localhost:11434/api/show with the model set to glm-5.3-flash:cloud returns a thinking object. In the provided response, the available values are low, high, and max, while max is identified as the default.

Thinking controls and their defaults can also be viewed directly on ollama.com for cloud models.

## Apple Silicon with MLX

Nemotron H vision models are now supported on Apple Silicon with MLX. This adds Apple Silicon support for using those vision models through the specified MLX implementation.

## macOS App and Pulls

Ollama’s macOS app changes how closed windows behave when the application is activated. Windows that a user has closed will no longer reopen simply because the app is activated.

The release also includes a fix for model pulls from HuggingFace. Together with the macOS window correction, this addresses two operational issues affecting model use.

The full changelog covers the changes between v0.34.2 and v0.34.3.

dcb36cccbd64a05d.bodyJa:
複数の大手出版社が、自社の記事やコンテンツをGoogleが人工知能（AI）モデルの学習に無断で利用したとして、著作権侵害を訴える新たな訴訟を提起した。メディア業界とAI開発企業の法的対立がさらに拡大しており、今後のAI開発のあり方に影響を及ぼす可能性がある。

訴訟の争点となっているのは、大規模言語モデル（LLM）の学習プロセスだ。生成AIは、インターネット上に公開された膨大なテキストや画像を取り込んで学習し、文章生成や要約などの能力を獲得する。出版社側は、こうした学習データに自社の著作物が許諾なく含まれ、対価も支払われていないと主張しているとみられる。特に、Googleが検索結果にAIによる回答を直接提示する「AI Overviews」のような仕組みは、ユーザーが元記事にアクセスしなくなり、出版社の広告収入や購読収入を損なうとの懸念が根強い。

同様の訴訟は近年相次いでいる。米New York Timesは2023年末にOpenAIとMicrosoftを提訴し、作家や報道機関による集団訴訟も各国で続いている。一方で、一部の出版社はライセンス契約による共存の道を選んでおり、OpenAIやGoogleは複数のメディアと有料の提携を結んでいる。訴訟と提携という二つの潮流が並行して進んでいる点が、現在の状況の特徴と言える。

AI企業側はこれまで、公開情報の学習は米著作権法の「フェアユース（公正利用）」に該当すると主張してきた。しかし、その解釈が生成AIの文脈でどこまで通用するかは裁判所の判断が定まっておらず、今回の訴訟も含めて司法の結論が業界全体の基準を左右する可能性がある。

Googleが今回の提訴にどのような反論を示すかは現時点で不明だが、判決や和解の内容次第では、学習データの調達方法やライセンス料の相場、さらにはAI製品の設計そのものにまで波及することも考えられる。日本を含む各国でも著作権とAIをめぐる議論が活発化しており、今回の動きは国際的な制度設計の行方を占う一つの指標となりそうだ。
dcb36cccbd64a05d.bodyEn:
A coalition of major publishers has filed a new lawsuit against Google, alleging that the company used their copyrighted articles and other content to train its artificial intelligence systems without permission or compensation. The complaint adds to a rapidly expanding body of litigation between media organizations and AI developers, and it underscores how unresolved questions about training data are becoming a central legal and commercial battleground for the technology industry.

At the heart of the case is a dispute that has recurred across the sector: whether the ingestion of copyrighted material to build large language models constitutes infringement, or whether it falls under fair use and similar exceptions. The publishers argue that their journalism represents a significant and costly investment, and that Google appears to have benefited from that work to develop products that can summarize, paraphrase, or otherwise reproduce information without directing traffic or revenue back to the original sources. Google has typically defended such practices by pointing to fair use doctrine and arguing that training models on publicly available text is transformative rather than a substitute for the original works.

The complaint reportedly focuses on both the training process and the downstream products that rely on it. Modern AI systems are built by processing enormous volumes of text, and news content is often considered especially valuable because it is timely, factual, and professionally edited. Publishers contend that features such as AI-generated overviews in search results can answer user questions directly, potentially reducing the clicks that news sites depend on for advertising and subscription income. That concern connects the legal argument about how models are trained to a broader business anxiety about how AI-driven interfaces may reshape the flow of readers across the open web.

This is not an isolated action. The suit follows a series of high-profile cases, most notably The New York Times' litigation against OpenAI and Microsoft, along with claims brought by authors, artists, music labels, and other publishers against companies including Anthropic, Stability AI, and Meta. Courts in the United States and elsewhere have begun to weigh these disputes, but there is not yet a settled body of precedent, and outcomes have so far been mixed. Some rulings have leaned toward fair-use arguments in narrow contexts, while others have allowed infringement claims to proceed, leaving the overall legal landscape unresolved.

Running alongside the courtroom fights is a parallel track of commercial negotiation. Several AI firms have signed licensing deals with publishers, agreeing to pay for access to archives and ongoing content. OpenAI, for example, has struck agreements with a number of news organizations, and Google itself has pursued content partnerships in various forms. These arrangements suggest that at least part of the industry is moving toward a licensing model, even as litigation seeks to establish whether such licensing is legally required in the first place. The new lawsuit can be read, in part, as an effort to strengthen publishers' bargaining position by pressing the argument that unlicensed training is unlawful.

For readers less familiar with the underlying technology, the core concepts help explain the stakes. Large language models learn statistical patterns from vast text datasets, and the quality and provenance of that data materially affect performance. Because the models do not simply store and retrieve articles verbatim, questions about when output infringes copyright, and how to attribute or trace training data, remain technically and legally complex. Related debates include the use of retrieval-augmented generation, which pulls in live web content, and the growing interest in "opt-out" mechanisms and machine-readable licensing signals that would let publishers control how their material is used.

The financial and strategic implications are considerable. If courts ultimately require broad licensing, AI developers could face higher costs and more constrained access to high-quality data, which may influence how future systems are built and priced. If fair-use defenses prevail, publishers may need to rely more heavily on negotiated deals and product partnerships. Either way, the outcome is likely to shape the relationship between the news industry and AI platforms for years to come. Google has not conceded the claims, and the litigation is expected to be lengthy, meaning any definitive resolution, whether through the courts or a settlement, appears to be some distance away.

e305871a692415df.bodyJa:
家庭向けの複数 GPU 環境で大規模言語モデル（LLM）を高速に動かす需要が高まる中、量子化推論ライブラリ exllamav3 の Tensor Parallel（TP）を、12GB の Blackwell 世代 GPU 2 枚と WSL2 という制約下で動作させるまでの記録が公開された。VRAM の限られた民生 GPU を組み合わせて実用的な推論環境を構築する上での、実践的な知見として参考になる内容だ。

exllamav3 は、EXL3 形式などの量子化モデルを効率よく扱う推論エンジンで、単一 GPU に載りきらないモデルを複数 GPU に分割する Tensor Parallel に対応する。TP は各層の行列演算を複数デバイスに分散し、全 GPU が並列に計算した結果を集約（gather や all-reduce）することでスループットを高める手法だが、GPU 間の高速な通信が前提となる。

ここで壁となったのが NCCL（NVIDIA Collective Communications Library）だ。TP の集団通信で標準的に使われる NCCL は、Windows 上の WSL2 環境では GPU 間の Peer-to-Peer 通信を十分にサポートしておらず、そのまま動作させることが難しいとされる。記事では NCCL に依存しない通信経路へ切り替えるといった回避策で対処している。

さらに、GPU 間で計算結果を集める gather カーネルにおいて、同期の不備に起因すると見られるレースコンディション（競合状態）が発生し、出力が破損する問題にも直面したという。こうした競合は、複数ストリームやデバイスをまたぐ処理でタイミング依存の不具合として現れやすく、適切な同期を挿入することで安定動作にこぎ着けたとしている。

背景として、NVIDIA の Blackwell 世代は新しいアーキテクチャゆえにドライバや CUDA、各種ライブラリの対応が発展途上で、既存コードがそのまま動かない場面も少なくない。WSL2 は Windows 上で Linux 向けの機械学習ツールを扱える利便性がある一方、ネイティブ Linux と比べてハードウェア寄りの機能に制約が残る場合がある。llama.cpp や vLLM など他の推論基盤でもマルチ GPU 構成の相性問題は報告されており、環境固有の検証が依然として重要であることを示す事例と言えるだろう。
e305871a692415df.bodyEn:
Running large language models locally on consumer hardware increasingly means combining more than one mid-range GPU, and this write-up walks through the practical obstacles of doing exactly that: enabling exllamav3's Tensor Parallel inference across two 12 GB Blackwell-generation cards inside a WSL2 environment. The exercise matters because it sits at the intersection of three trends — the rise of quantized inference engines, the growing viability of multi-GPU setups for enthusiasts, and the reality that many hobbyists run their AI stack on Windows through the Windows Subsystem for Linux rather than on bare-metal Linux.

By way of background, exllamav3 is a high-performance inference library optimized for its EXL3 quantization format, designed to squeeze large models onto limited VRAM while retaining acceptable quality. Tensor Parallel, the technique at the center of this article, splits individual weight matrices across multiple GPUs so that each device handles a slice of every layer. This differs from simple layer-wise or pipeline splitting, where whole layers are assigned to separate cards. Tensor parallelism can improve throughput and lets a model that would not fit on a single 12 GB card span two of them, but it demands frequent, low-latency communication between the GPUs to combine partial results after each parallelized operation.

That communication requirement is where the first wall appears. Multi-GPU inference frameworks typically rely on NCCL, NVIDIA's Collective Communications Library, to handle the all-reduce and all-gather operations that stitch tensor-parallel shards back together. NCCL, however, is not fully supported under WSL2. The virtualized GPU path that WSL exposes does not provide the peer-to-peer and device-to-device transport features NCCL expects, so attempts to initialize an NCCL communicator inside WSL commonly fail or hang. The article frames this bluntly as the "NCCL is impossible on WSL" barrier, and it is a well-known limitation that has affected other projects attempting distributed workloads on the subsystem.

The workaround, as described, is to avoid NCCL entirely and route the cross-GPU synchronization through an alternative communication path. In practice this appears to mean falling back to a non-NCCL backend for the collective operations — for example, staging data through host memory or using a custom gather implementation rather than the library's optimized collectives. This sidesteps the incompatibility but shifts the burden onto exllamav3's own kernels to move and combine tensors between the two Blackwell devices, which is where the second problem surfaces.

That second issue is a race condition in the gather kernel. When partial outputs from each GPU are gathered and recombined, correct results depend on all contributing operations completing before the gathered buffer is read. If synchronization is missing or incorrectly placed, one GPU can begin reading or writing shared data before the other has finished, producing corrupted activations, non-deterministic output, or outright crashes. The article documents diagnosing and addressing this timing hazard, likely by adding or correcting stream synchronization so that the gather step waits for the relevant kernels and memory transfers to finish. Race conditions of this kind are notoriously intermittent, which makes them difficult to reproduce and easy to mistake for other faults, so pinning the behavior to the gather path is a meaningful part of the story.

The Blackwell context adds another layer of nuance. As a newer architecture, Blackwell cards can require recent CUDA toolkits, driver versions, and framework builds, and support in inference libraries may still be maturing. Combining bleeding-edge hardware with the constraints of WSL2 compounds the risk that a given code path has not been widely tested, which is one reason low-level bugs like the gather race can go unnoticed until someone runs this specific configuration.

For readers weighing a similar build, the takeaways are pragmatic rather than universal. Dual 12 GB GPUs can serve as an affordable route to running larger quantized models with tensor parallelism, but the software path is not turnkey on WSL2, and users should expect to substitute non-NCCL communication and to verify output correctness carefully. Those who can run native Linux may avoid the NCCL limitation altogether, and anyone attempting this on Windows should treat the described fixes as a starting point that may shift as exllamav3 and Blackwell support continue to evolve.

069f1838583b56ab.bodyJa:
## AIの独り言

Claude CodeやGitHub Copilotに作業を頼むと、コードを出す前に、エラーの確認や調査方針を言葉にすることがあります。この「独り言」には、問題解決の進め方や判断根拠が含まれており、経験の浅いエンジニアが思考力を鍛える材料になると説明されています。

## コードだけを見る

新人エンジニアは途中の出力をスクロールで読み飛ばし、最後に示されるコードだけを見がちです。しかし、それでは修正結果は得られても、なぜその箇所を調べ、どの情報から原因を絞り込んだのかという過程を捨てることになります。

先輩が短時間でバグを直した場合、周囲から見えるのは直ったという結果だけです。判断過程は本人の頭の中にあり、無意識に行われているため、尋ねても「なんとなく」としか説明されないことがあります。AIエージェントは作業過程を言語化する設計であり、その判断に相当する内容を日本語で追えるとされています。

## エージェントモード

GitHub Copilotで独り言が見えるのは、チャットやエージェントモードを利用しているときで、タブ補完では表示されません。エージェントモードで簡単なバグ修正を頼み、コードが出る前の出力を観察することで、この違いを体感できると説明されています。

## バグ修正の流れ

典型例では、まずエラーメッセージ全体を確認します。TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined であれば、変数がどこでundefinedになるのかを特定し、呼び出し元を検索します。スタックトレースでは最下部だけを見るのではなく、自分のコードが最初に登場する行を見る、という着眼点も示されています。

重要なのは、出力された修正コードをそのまま使うことだけではありません。確認、切り分け、検索、判断という流れを読み、どの情報を手掛かりに次の行動を選んだのかを追うことに、AIの独り言を読む意味があります。
069f1838583b56ab.bodyEn:
## AI Reasoning Traces

AI reasoning traces contain problem-solving approaches and the rationale behind decisions, but junior engineers often scroll past them and focus only on the final code. Reading this running commentary can help engineers develop judgment by showing how a problem is examined before a solution is produced.

When Claude Code or GitHub Copilot is asked to perform a task, the AI may describe what it is doing before returning code. In GitHub Copilot, this commentary is visible in chat and agent mode, but not in tab completion.

## Problem-Solving Logic

A typical debugging trace begins by checking the complete error message. For a TypeError stating that properties of undefined cannot be read, the AI may first identify where the relevant variable becomes undefined and then search for its caller.

Another example is the handling of a stack trace. The described approach is not simply to inspect its final line, but to find the first line where the engineer’s own code appears. The value lies in seeing this sequence of attention and investigation, not only the resulting fix.

## Decision Rationale

When a skilled engineer fixes a bug quickly, a junior engineer usually sees only the corrected result. The reasons for choosing a particular place to inspect or a particular path through the code remain inside the experienced engineer’s head. Those decisions may also be difficult to explain afterward because they are made unconsciously.

AI agents, by contrast, work while expressing the process in language. Their commentary therefore presents, in Japanese, decisions corresponding to the kinds of judgments an experienced engineer may make without consciously describing them.

## Engineering Judgment

For experienced engineers, this output may look like familiar work being performed quickly. For less experienced engineers, it can serve as a visible account of a capable problem-solving process that would normally remain hidden.

The practical recommendation is to avoid copying only the answer and to read the AI’s commentary as well. Asking an agent to fix a simple bug and observing the output before the code appears provides a direct way to examine that reasoning process.

210d46dfe150a20f.bodyJa:
大規模言語モデル（LLM）を単なる文章生成器ではなく、外部ツールを呼び出して自律的にタスクを遂行する「エージェント」として活用する動きが加速している。Hugging Faceのブログは、オープンなLLMがこうしたエージェント用途にどこまで耐えうるかを、自社で用意したツール環境を使って評価する実践的な枠組みを紹介している。実務でモデルを選ぶ開発者にとって、性能を見極める具体的な指針となる内容だ。

エージェント的な処理では、モデルが状況を判断し、適切なタイミングで検索やコード実行、API呼び出しといったツールを選択・連携させる能力が問われる。単発の質問応答とは異なり、複数ステップにわたる推論や、途中で得た結果を踏まえた計画修正が必要になる。そのため従来の知識量や文章品質を測るベンチマークだけでは、実際のワークフローでの使い勝手を十分に反映できないという課題があった。

記事が提案するのは、公開データセットに頼るのではなく、自社の実タスクに即したカスタムツールと評価環境を構築するアプローチだ。ツール呼び出しの正確さ、引数の指定ミス、複数ツールを跨ぐ処理の成功率などを計測することで、モデルごとの得手不得手を可視化できる。汎用的なリーダーボードの順位が、必ずしも自分たちのユースケースでの実力と一致するとは限らないため、こうした独自評価には一定の合理性があると見られる。

背景には、エージェント開発を支えるツール群の成熟がある。Hugging FaceはsmolagentsやTransformers Agentsといったライブラリを提供しており、LangChainやLlamaIndexなど周辺エコシステムも活発だ。評価の分野では、Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboardやτ-benchのように、ツール利用能力に特化した指標も登場している。オープンモデル側でもQwenやLlama、Mistral系などが関数呼び出し対応を強化しており、クローズドなモデルとの差は用途によっては縮まりつつある可能性がある。

もっとも、独自ベンチマークの構築にはタスク設計や採点基準の整備といった手間が伴い、結果の再現性や公平性をどう担保するかという論点も残る。それでも、コスト管理やデータのプライバシー、オンプレミス運用を重視する現場では、オープンモデルを自前の基準で検証する意義は大きい。エージェント実装を検討する開発者にとって、まず小さな評価環境を用意し、候補モデルを横並びで比較することが、堅実な第一歩になりそうだ。
210d46dfe150a20f.bodyEn:
As large language models increasingly move from generating text to taking actions, developers face a pressing question: are today's open models capable enough to serve as reliable agents? This article outlines a practical framework for benchmarking open LLMs on agentic tasks using custom tooling, an approach that matters because generic leaderboard scores rarely predict how a model will behave inside a specific application with its own tools, data, and constraints.

Agentic behavior refers to a model's ability to reason about a goal, decide which tools to call, interpret the results, and iterate until the task is complete. Unlike single-turn question answering, this requires the model to plan across multiple steps, format tool calls correctly, recover from errors, and know when to stop. These are distinct skills, and a model that excels at conversational benchmarks may still struggle to chain several function calls together reliably. That gap is precisely why teams building real agent workflows need evaluation methods that mirror their production environment rather than relying solely on public benchmarks.

The core idea presented is to construct a benchmark around your own tools instead of borrowing an abstract test suite. In practice, this means defining a set of functions the agent can invoke, such as a search endpoint, a database query, a calculator, or an internal API, and then writing tasks whose successful completion depends on calling those tools in the right sequence with the right arguments. Each task is paired with a verifiable success condition, so scoring can be automated rather than left to subjective judgment. This design keeps the evaluation grounded in the actual capabilities the application depends on.

Several technical details make such a framework robust. First, tool-calling formats vary between models: some are trained to emit structured JSON, others use specific chat templates or special tokens, and mismatches here often cause failures that have nothing to do with reasoning ability. A fair benchmark must normalize for these differences or test each model with its native format. Second, evaluation should separate types of failure, distinguishing between a model that chose the wrong tool, one that called the right tool with malformed arguments, and one that reasoned correctly but hit a parsing error. Tracking these categories helps teams understand whether a shortfall is fixable through prompting and schema tweaks or reflects a deeper capability limit. Third, metrics typically extend beyond a single pass rate to include the number of steps taken, token cost, and latency, since an agent that reaches the answer inefficiently may be impractical to deploy at scale.

The broader context is a rapidly maturing ecosystem of tools that make this kind of testing feasible. Hugging Face has invested in agent-oriented libraries, and frameworks such as smolagents, LangChain, and LlamaIndex provide the scaffolding to connect models to tools. The Model Context Protocol, introduced to standardize how models access external tools and data, is one industry move that appears aimed at reducing the format fragmentation described above. On the evaluation side, public efforts like the Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard and various agent benchmarks offer useful reference points, though the article's argument is that these should complement, not replace, a custom suite tailored to your domain.

For teams choosing among open models, the practical guidance is to treat model selection as an empirical exercise. Candidates might include instruction-tuned releases from families such as Llama, Qwen, Mistral, or specialized function-calling variants, and the right choice is likely to depend on the specific tools and task complexity rather than on parameter count alone. Smaller models that are well matched to a narrow toolset can sometimes outperform larger general-purpose ones while costing less to run, which is especially relevant for local or self-hosted deployments where hardware budgets are fixed.

Building an in-house benchmark does carry costs. It requires effort to author representative tasks, maintain them as tools evolve, and guard against the evaluation becoming stale or overfit. There is also a risk of measuring what is easy to measure rather than what matters most to users. Still, the reproducibility and relevance of a custom harness generally outweigh these drawbacks for production systems. The overarching message is that agentic capability is not a single number but a profile of behaviors, and measuring it against your own environment is the most dependable way to decide whether an open model is ready for the job.

5fa22693df37fad2.bodyEn:
## Zed v1.20.2

Zed v1.20.2 addresses payment-error handling for third-party model providers and a conflict involving snippet extensions. The changes matter because users can now see the provider’s original payment error, while different snippet extensions for the same language no longer cancel each other.

The release was published on September 17, 2026. Its associated commit was created on GitHub.com and signed with GitHub’s verified signature.

## Payment errors

Previously, payment errors from non-Zed model providers could incorrectly prompt users to upgrade to Zed Pro. That prompt replaced the original error message from the provider, making the source of the payment problem less clear.

With v1.20.2, Zed displays the original provider error instead of steering the user toward a Zed Pro upgrade. This allows users to identify that the failure comes from the third-party model provider and to see the provider’s own description of the issue. The payment-error correction is tracked as issue #64354.

The change is specifically about how these provider-side payment failures are presented. It corrects the misleading upgrade prompt and preserves the original error information rather than substituting a Zed Pro message.

## Snippet extensions

The release also fixes an issue affecting different snippet extensions associated with the same language. Before this correction, those extensions could cancel each other.

Zed v1.20.2 changes that behavior so different snippet extensions for one language no longer cancel one another. This fix is tracked as issue #64314.

Together, the two fixes focus on presenting the correct payment failure information and preventing conflicts between snippet extensions that target the same language.

7ff96fa315614a27.bodyEn:
## Cursor Automations

Cursor Automations now adds the /automate skill, new GitHub and Slack triggers, and computer-use support. These capabilities expand how always-on agents can automate repetitive developer workflows and save time.

The release brings automation creation closer to the work performed in local agent sessions while adding more ways to start workflows and generate demonstrations or artifacts.

## /automate skill

The /automate skill lets users create an automation directly within a local agent session. To set one up, the user describes the task to automate in natural language.

Cursor then configures the automation’s triggers, instructions, and tools. This approach allows the automation to be defined through a task description rather than requiring each of those elements to be set up separately.

## GitHub and Slack triggers

An automation can now be started by reacting to a Slack message with a specified emoji. Cursor uses this capability to trigger particular automations directly from Slack.

The release also adds support for five GitHub triggers for automations. The individual triggers are not specified, but the addition broadens the available GitHub-based starting points.

New templates are available in the Cursor marketplace to help users get started. They cover triaging failed GitHub Actions and automatically fixing PR review comments.

## Computer-use support

Cloud agents launched by automations can now use a dedicated computer to produce demonstrations of their work or generate artifacts. The computer-use tool is enabled by default for every automation.

To have an agent include a demonstration of its work, users can add that requirement to the automation’s instructions. This connects the agent’s computer use directly to the requested output.

To access these additions, users need to update Cursor to the latest version. Further information is available in the documentation.

801b24fe3b176db2.bodyJa:
AIコーディング支援ツール「Claude Code」を使っていて、トークン量の割に請求額が抑えられていると感じたことはないだろうか。その背景には「プロンプトキャッシュ（prompt caching）」と呼ばれる仕組みが深く関わっており、これを理解することがコスト最適化の第一歩になる。

プロンプトキャッシュは、Anthropicが提供するAPI機能の一つだ。大規模言語モデル（LLM）は本来、リクエストのたびに入力トークン全体を処理する必要があるが、コーディング作業では同じシステムプロンプトやファイル内容、会話履歴が繰り返し送られる場面が多い。キャッシュはこの共通部分をサーバー側に一時保存し、次回以降の再処理を省くことで、応答速度と課金を同時に改善する狙いがある。

課金構造を具体的に見ると、キャッシュには「書き込み」と「読み込み」で異なるトークン単価が設定されている。一般に、キャッシュへの書き込みは通常の入力トークンよりやや割高になる一方、キャッシュからの読み込みは大幅に安価とされる。Anthropicの公開情報では、キャッシュ読み込みが通常入力の10分の1程度になる場合があるとされ、繰り返しの多い長時間セッションほど恩恵が大きくなる。

Claude Codeがこのキャッシュを積極的に活用しているとみられる点は重要だ。プロジェクト全体のコンテキストを保持しながら対話を続ける同ツールの性質上、キャッシュが効かなければ入力トークンが膨張し、コストが跳ね上がる可能性がある。逆に言えば、キャッシュヒットが続く限り、実際の請求はトークン量から素朴に想像するより低く抑えられる。

ただしキャッシュには有効期限（TTL）があり、標準では数分程度とされる。一定時間操作が途切れると失効し、再度書き込みコストが発生する点には留意したい。作業を細切れにするより、集中して連続的に進めるほうがキャッシュ効率の面では有利になると考えられる。

同様の仕組みはOpenAIやGoogleなど他社のAPIでも導入が進んでおり、プロンプトキャッシュは今やLLM活用のコスト設計における前提知識になりつつある。Claude Codeの請求明細を眺める際も、キャッシュ関連の項目に目を向けることで、料金の増減を合理的に説明できるようになるだろう。
801b24fe3b176db2.bodyEn:
Prompt caching has quietly become one of the most consequential factors in the cost of running Claude Code, Anthropic's terminal-based agentic coding assistant. For developers who use the tool intensively, understanding how caching interacts with token billing is often the difference between a predictable monthly bill and an unexpectedly large one, which is why it deserves closer attention than most usage guides give it.

At its core, prompt caching addresses a structural inefficiency in how large language models handle repeated context. Every time an API request is made, the model normally reprocesses the full prompt from scratch, including system instructions, tool definitions, and any accumulated conversation history. In an agentic coding session, that context can be enormous and largely unchanged from one turn to the next. Caching lets the provider store the processed representation of a prompt prefix so that later requests can reuse it rather than recomputing it.

The economics are what make this important. Anthropic's pricing separates tokens into several categories: standard input tokens, cache write tokens, and cache read tokens. Writing to the cache typically costs more than a normal input token, commonly around 25 percent more for the default five-minute cache window, because the system must process and store the content. Reading from the cache, however, is dramatically cheaper, often priced at roughly one-tenth of the standard input rate. Output tokens are billed separately and are unaffected by caching. There is also a longer one-hour cache option, which appears to carry a higher write premium in exchange for a longer time-to-live.

This asymmetry explains why prompt caching sits at the center of Claude Code's billing structure. A coding session repeatedly sends a large, stable block of context—the system prompt, tool schemas, files that have been read, and prior exchanges—on top of a small amount of new input. Without caching, that entire block would be billed at full input rates on every turn. With caching, the bulk of it is written once and then read back at a fraction of the cost for the duration of the cache window. Because interactive coding tends to produce frequent, closely spaced requests, cache hits are common, and the savings compound over the length of a session.

Understanding this behavior has practical consequences. Actions that invalidate or fail to reuse the cache tend to be the expensive ones. Long pauses that let the cache expire, edits that change an early part of the context and therefore break the reusable prefix, or workflows that repeatedly restructure the beginning of a prompt can all force fresh cache writes. Keeping stable content at the front of the context and volatile content toward the end is likely to improve hit rates, since caching generally works on shared prefixes.

It helps to place this in the broader landscape. Prompt caching is not unique to Anthropic; OpenAI and Google have introduced comparable mechanisms, and the general trend across providers is toward pricing that rewards reusing context rather than resending it. Claude Code competes with tools such as GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Aider, and OpenAI's Codex-style agents, many of which grapple with the same cost pressure from large, repeated context windows. For subscription-based access through Claude's Pro and Max plans, the caching mechanics are handled behind the scenes, but for developers working directly against the API or through pay-as-you-go billing, they translate directly into money.

The prerequisite concept worth emphasizing is that tokens, not requests, are the unit of cost, and that not all tokens are priced equally. Once that distinction is clear, the value of caching becomes intuitive: the goal is to maximize inexpensive cache reads while minimizing full-price input processing and unnecessary cache writes. Anthropic exposes cache-related token counts in its API responses, so usage can be measured rather than guessed.

For teams budgeting around agentic coding, the takeaway is that cost optimization is less about limiting how much you use Claude Code and more about structuring interactions so the cache does as much work as possible. Treating prompt caching as a first-class part of the workflow, rather than an implementation detail, appears to be the most reliable path to keeping API spending in check.

11814c13f8eb0837.bodyJa:
固定された画面に作業を合わせるのではなく、望むワークフローに沿ってインターフェースを形作れるのが、GitHub Copilot appの「キャンバス」です。利用者とエージェントが同じカスタム画面を双方向に操作し、用途に合った作業環境を構成できます。

## キャンバス

キャンバスは「canvas extension」とも呼ばれ、利用者とエージェントが共有するカスタマイズ可能なインターフェースです。カンバンボード、課題整理用のボード、リリースチェックリスト、ダッシュボード、フォーム、表計算などとして構成できます。決められた種類の画面に作業を当てはめるのではなく、実際の作業方法に合わせてUIを形作るという考え方です。独自の作業手順を効率化したいチームに役立つとされています。

## 双方向の操作

キャンバスは双方向に操作できるため、エージェントは作業を進めながら画面の内容を更新できます。一方、利用者もボタン、カード、フィルターなどの操作要素を使って変更を加えられます。エージェントからの更新を表示するだけの画面ではなく、双方が同じ画面に働きかけられる仕組みです。これは、共有されたライブホワイトボードを一緒に使うような操作感として説明されています。

## 作成方法

キャンバスを作る際に、利用者がコードを書いたり、画面を手作業でデザインしたりする必要はありません。まずエージェントのセッションを開き、「/create-canvas」スキルを入力します。そのうえで、作りたい画面や実現したい内容を平易な英語で説明します。これにより、目的とするワークフローを起点として、必要なインターフェースを構成できます。
11814c13f8eb0837.bodyEn:
## GitHub Copilot app canvases

Canvases in the GitHub Copilot app offer a way to build an interface around the workflow a user wants, rather than fitting that work into a fixed set of screens. This matters for teams that want to tailor custom workflows to their own needs.

A canvas, also called a canvas extension, is a customizable interface shared by the user and the agent. Its structure can reflect the work being performed instead of requiring the user to adapt that work to a predetermined interface.

## A customizable interface

A canvas can take several forms, including a kanban board, an issue triage board, a release checklist, a dashboard, a form, or a spreadsheet. These options allow the interface to be shaped according to how the user or team works.

The canvas is bidirectional. The agent can update the interface while it works, while the user can also make changes through buttons, cards, filters, and other controls. The result is comparable to using a live shared whiteboard: both sides interact with the same customizable space rather than working through separate views.

This shared editing model means that a canvas is not simply a static display of information. It is an interface in which the agent’s updates and the user’s direct actions can both affect the workflow.

## Create a canvas

Creating a canvas does not require coding or manual interface design. The user starts by opening an agent session and entering the /create-canvas skill.

The next step is to describe the desired canvas in plain English. That description can specify the workflow and the kind of interface needed, such as a board, checklist, dashboard, form, or spreadsheet. The GitHub Copilot app then uses that request to create a canvas shaped around the described work.

chat.en: Yes. Teams can tailor kanban boards, issue triage, release checklists, spreadsheets, and more to streamline their own workflows.
